Response: The draft EIS raises this issue in response to certain allegations made in the initial pleadings. This argument is identified and the environmental effects which would result should the proposition prove valid are delineated. After examining these arguments in some detail, the impact statement concludes that there is not sufficient data available to show a nexus between commercial zone expansion and urban sprawl. In addition, while certain comments to the draft claim that urban sprawl will occur as a direct result of expansion of the commercial zone, these assertions are not supported by any new evidence, and remain merely disagreements with the conclusions of the impact statement. Comment: On the issue of urban sprawl the Commission makes flatly contradictory statements concerning the effects of the population/ mileage formula (Local and Short Haul Carriers National Conference). Response: See introductory remarks to section II of the impact statement.
Comment: The EDA survey of industrial location determinants suggests that the location of a plantsite within a given terminal area may be a prime determinant of plantsite selection. Even though the Commission asserts this is not so, the impact statement should discuss what relationship there is between location determinants and commercial zones. (Lakeville.)
